title: High-Cardinality Lock Contention in Histograms
pattern: Creating thousands of high-precision histogram buckets and wrapping the entire metric array in a single mutex lock updated synchronously on the hot path.
why_bad: High-cardinality buckets cause massive cache line misses, and locking the entire structure on every transaction blocks parallel worker threads from doing real work, severely degrading performance (observer effect).
detection: Look for synchronous locks (`Mutex`, `RwLock`) wrapping multi-bucket arrays updated inside high-frequency execution loops.
strength: Strong` — introduces high-frequency locking overhead on the telemetry path.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Chapter 13.5, p. 212-214.
